name: US dollar
summary: Dollar index 103.8 on 18 Nov, a 52-week high, up 5.1% over three months, crossing the 5% Watch line
state: The DXY dollar index stood at 103.8 on 18 Nov, its highest in a year, up 5.1% over three months and 0.6% on the week, crossing the 5% three-month Watch line (Yahoo Finance). Trading Economics said on 16 Nov the rise to a near 20-month high came as markets priced a quarter-point Fed rise in December. The level remains well inside the 90–108 range and no dollar funding strain was found.
for_you: A stronger dollar raises the local cost of dollar-priced goods such as fuel and commodities, and adds pressure on countries and firms with dollar debts.

sources.title: Trading Economics — Dollar Index Rises to 20-Month High

why: The dollar is the world's funding currency; violent moves squeeze emerging markets and anyone with dollar debts.
drivers: Fed vs other central banks, safe-haven demand, trade policy, reserve diversification.

rubric.alert: DXY moved > 8% in 3 months, or dollar funding stress (Fed swap lines drawn materially).
rubric.watch: DXY moved 5–8% in 3 months, or outside 90–108.
rubric.normal: DXY moved < 5% over 3 months and is between 90 and 108.
